_about.purpose: Pins extractHitLikelihoodFeatures() — the three numbers the whole estimate is computed from. A drift here is worse than a drift in the model: the walker would still reproduce XGBoost exactly while being handed a different alignment than the user uploaded.
contract: num_seqs = non-empty sequence records; falls back to the tree's tip count (commas + 1) when the alignment yields none
num_sites = floor(length of the FIRST sequence / 3), i.e. CODONS, not nucleotides
median_pos_dist = numpy-style median of the STRICTLY POSITIVE branch lengths in the newick (mean of the middle two when the count is even); 0.0 is the 'none were parsed' sentinel, never a measurement
_about.provenance: Each `expected` is hand-derived from the contract above and the derivation is written out in `why`, so every number in this file can be checked by reading it rather than by running the code it tests. They are NOT recorded outputs of extractHitLikelihoodFeatures().
_about.clip_note: Unclipped on purpose. MODEL_INPUT_CLIP (median floor 0.001) lives at the scoring boundary; flooring here would make checkFeatureDomain's 'missing' branch unreachable and score a topology-only tree as if it were a measurement.

cases.name: fasta_with_lengths
cases.why: 4 records; 12 nt / 3 = 4 codons; branch lengths sorted 0.05 0.1 0.15 0.2 0.25 0.3 -> even count, median = (0.15 + 0.2) / 2 = 0.175

cases.name: fasta_no_positive_lengths
cases.why: 3 records; 12 nt / 3 = 4 codons; a topology-only tree has no ':' at all, so the positive-length list is empty and the median is the 0.0 sentinel

cases.name: fasta_scientific_notation
cases.why: 2 records; 15 nt / 3 = 5 codons; both exponent spellings must parse -> 0.015 and 0.003, median = (0.003 + 0.015) / 2 = 0.009. A parser that missed the 'E' form would silently return the 0.0 sentinel here rather than erroring.

cases.name: nexus_input
cases.why: NEXUS branch: 3 MATRIX rows (the last keeps its content and drops the terminating ';'); 9 nt / 3 = 3 codons; lengths sorted 0.1 0.4 0.5 0.6, median = (0.4 + 0.5) / 2 = 0.45

cases.name: fasta_wrapped_lines
cases.alignment:
>long1
ATGACT
GATCCC
GGGAAA
>long2
ATGACA
GATCCC
GGGAAT
cases.why: Wrapped records must be joined before measuring: 18 nt / 3 = 6 codons, not 6 nt / 3 = 2. Median of two lengths = (0.12 + 0.34) / 2 = 0.23

cases.name: fasta_headers_only_falls_back_to_tip_count
cases.why: No sequence lines, so 0 records and 0 codons; num_seqs falls back to the tree's tip count = commas + 1 = 4. This path exists so a parse that recovers taxa but no residues still reports the right shape; it is reachable and previously untested. num_sites 0 is what makes checkFeatureDomain refuse it (below-min), so the fallback cannot fabricate a scorable row.

cases.name: negative_branch_lengths_are_dropped_not_averaged
cases.why: 3 records; 15 nt / 3 = 5 codons; the median is over STRICTLY POSITIVE lengths only -> [0.2, 0.4], median = (0.2 + 0.4) / 2. Written as the exact float64 result of that sum rather than 0.3, because the test compares within 1e-12 and 0.2 + 0.4 is not 0.6. Including the -0.5 would give 0.2; a filter on `>= 0` rather than `> 0` would also give 0.2 on a tree carrying a 0.0.
